 JOHANNESBURG (AP) — Simon Harmer ran through Bangladesh's tail and South Africa knocked off the 12 runs required to win the first test by nine wickets on Thursday, taking a 1-0 lead in the teams' two-match cricket test series.
 Resuming on 100-5 at the Wanderers, Bangladesh's lower-order batters couldn't handle the off-spin of Harmer, who took four of the remaining five wickets to help dismiss the tourists for 168 and have figures of 6-51.
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 It revived memories of Harmer taking 6-16 on Day 5 of the series-clinching victory over Australia last month.
 The Proteas lost first-innings century-maker Marques Ackerman — for a second-ball duck — on the way to reaching their target before lunch, at 12-1. Soon after getting bowled off a no-ball, Aiden Markram (8 not out) scored the winning run.
 South Africa dethroned Australia for the top spot in the ICC test team rankings with that series win last month and is the reigning world test champion.
 In Harmer it has a 37-year-old player enjoying a renaissance in a test career that was drifting until a year ago, when he returned after a two-and-a-half-year absence and is now a reliable match-winner.
 Having already removed Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mahfijul Islam late in Day 4, Harmer took the final four wickets of the match in his brilliant four-over burst that came after overnight batter Litton Das got an inside edge and played onto his own stumps off Kagiso Rabada (3-46).
 Mushfiqur Rahim added 34 runs to his overnight 5 before gloving Harmer to a close fielder, for a dismissal that was only given after the Proteas reviewed a not-out call.
 In his next over, Harmer had Mehidy Hasan Miraz stumped for 4, before removing Hasan Mahmud (4) and Ebadot Hossain (0) in consecutive balls to wrap up the innings.
 Despite making 400 in the first innings after winning the toss, Bangladesh barely avoided an innings defeat.
 The second test is at Centurion starting on Monday, and South Africa will head into it atop the points table in the World Test Championship for 2025-27.
